headline: Gratitude turns what we have into enough
universal_truth: The richest life isn't about having more—it's about appreciating more
fun_facts: Gratitude practices have been shown to increase happiness by 25% according to research by Dr. Robert Emmons
People who keep gratitude journals exercise more, have fewer physical symptoms, and feel better about their lives
Neuroimaging shows that gratitude activates the brain's reward pathways and increases activity in the hypothalamus, reducing stress
discussion_questions: What in your life do you take for granted that would be devastating to lose?
How might your daily experience change with more active gratitude?
Who in your life deserves more appreciation from you?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: There's a strange paradox: the more we have, the less we appreciate it. Hedonic adaptation ensures we normalize our blessings. Today we explore how to fight this drift—and why gratitude might be the most powerful happiness hack there is.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Studies show that gratitude is one of the strongest predictors of well-being—stronger than income, health, or even relationships. Why would simply appreciating what you have be so powerful?
cliff.prompt: Why is gratitude so powerful for well-being?

options.text: It shifts focus from lack to abundance
options.response: Exactly. Gratitude changes what you notice. And what you notice becomes your experienced reality.

options.text: It makes other people like you more
options.response: That's a benefit, but the real power is internal—gratitude transforms your relationship with your own life.

q1.title: The Adaptation Trap
q1.script: Hedonic adaptation is our tendency to return to a baseline happiness regardless of what happens to us. Win the lottery, get used to it. Lose a limb, adjust to it. This means acquiring more doesn't create lasting satisfaction. Appreciation does.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Adaptation Trap"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Gratitude Rewires the Brain
q2.script: Neuroscience reveals that practicing gratitude changes brain structure. It activates the hypothalamus and increases dopamine production. Over time, grateful people literally develop neural pathways that make appreciation easier.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: The Practice Effect
q3.script: Gratitude isn't just a feeling—it's a practice. Keeping a gratitude journal, expressing thanks to others, noticing small blessings—these behaviors compound. The more you practice, the more naturally grateful you become.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You already have enough to be grateful for. The question is whether you're paying attention to it. Gratitude isn't about ignoring problems—it's about seeing the whole picture, including the good.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's today's lesson on the power of appreciation. Tomorrow, we'll explore closing chapters well. Until then, notice something you've been taking for granted.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Gratitude Snapshot - The Taken-for-Granted List
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize and appreciate blessings that have become invisible through familiarity
growTrack.activity: List 5 things you'd desperately miss if they were gone: a person, a capability, a comfort, a relationship, an opportunity. Let yourself genuinely feel appreciation for each one.
